texts.facts: In this case, a Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred as DAR) was filed by police official concerned and in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, same is treated as Claim Petition under Section 166 (1) read with Section 166 (4) MV Act. It pertains to alleged accident of victim Bikash @ Vikas Kumar (hereinafter referred as deceased), by vehicle bearing (Car) Reg. No. DL 3CBU 3277 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle), driven by Mohd Sahid (hereinafter referred as R-1) and Vikas Kumar (Dar) vs Mohd. Sahid (17/19, Oia) on 20 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168524186/ 1 owned by Shameen Khan (hereinafter referred as R-2). 2. Preliminary information regarding accident in question was received at PS Okhla Industrial Area vide DD no. 67A on 13.01.2019 upon receipt of which HC Padam Singh along with Ct. Gurdayal proceeded to the spot of accident at F-27/5, Okhla Industrial Area-2, New Delhi where accidental Swift car bearing No. DL 3CBU 3277 along with its driver Shahid S/o Abdul Rashid were found present along with other public persons who informed that a pedestrian has been hit by the aforementioned vehicle and the injured has been shifted to hospital by PCR van. The car was stated to be damaged by public persons gathered there who also allegedly wanted to beat the driver, therefore, the said car along with its driver were sent to PS along with Ct. Gurdayal so as to ensure their safety. In the meanwhile, DD no. 7A was received from AIIMS where Vikash Kumar had taken the treatment and was discharged from emergency therefore, injured Vikash Kumar was not found present in the hospital upon visit by HC Padam Singh. Subsequently, injured came to the PS and gave his written complaint wherein he stated that he belongs to Distt. MACT No.147/20 Bikash Kumar @ Vikash Kumar Vs. Mohd. Sajid & Anr page 2 of 23 Munger Bihar and is tailor by profession. He stated that he was hit on 13.01.2019 at 10.15 PM in front of company office number F-27/5, Okhla Industrial Area (hereinafter called the spot of accident) while coming from community toilet near Sherawali Mandir by a speeding Swift car bearing No. DL 3CBU 3277 plying from A- Block, Okhla Phase-II on account of which he fell down and sustained injuries in his left leg. He stated that the driver was apprehended by public persons who revealed his name to be Sahid. Somebody called the PCR which shifted him to AIIMS Trauma Center where he was given treatment. He stated that the offending vehicle, being driven in rash and negligent manner by its driver, was responsible for causing the accident. Subsequently, FIR was registered on the basis statement of injured as well as the MLC. Offending vehicle was taken into police possession. Driver of offending vehicle was arrested and subsequently bailed out. Owner Shamim Khan was served with notice u/s 133 MV who confirmed that the vehicle was being driven by Mohd. Shahid on the date of accident and also revealed that the vehicle was not insured on the date of acident on account of which relevant provisions u/s 146/196 MV Act were added. Subsequently, on account of injuries opined as grievous, relevant penal provisions were substituted. Mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle was got conducted. Upon conclusion of investigation, charge sheet U/s 279/338 IPC was filed before concerned Ilaka MM whereas DAR was filed in this court. Reply: 3. On the very first date of hearing, both driver and owner appeared in person. Subsequently, they stopped appearing before the court and also chose not to file any reply. Therefore, their MACT No.147/20 Bikash Kumar @ Vikash Kumar Vs. Mohd. Sajid & Anr page 3 of 23 right to file reply was closed. Issues: 4. Issues were framed on the basis of pleadings of parties vide order dated 30.03.2021 which are as under: Vikas Kumar (Dar) vs Mohd. Sahid (17/19, Oia) on 20 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168524186/ 2 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 13.01.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL 3CBU 3277 being driven by R-1 and owned by R-2? OPP 2. To what amount of compensation the petitioner is entitled to claim and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. Evidence: 5. Matter was then listed for claimant evidence. However, no witness was produced on behalf of claimant. Interest of claimant was also directed to be closed w.e.f. 30.03.2021 till evidence is concluded. Last and final opportunity was granted vide order dated 17.11.2023 for conclusion of evidence, however, no witness was produced. Counsel for claimant stated that the matter may be decided on the basis of DAR and other material available on record and claimant evidence be considered closed. Since none was appearing on behalf of driver and owner, who chose not to contest the matter and even did not file reply, their Respondent Evidence was also closed.
